clips.label: no_swing
clips.notes: Hitter: 'Swing 2. Session, false positive 6m away.' Published 198.2 mph off four points that accelerate 3.3x and fit a parabola perfectly — the clip maxExitVeloMph and maxShortTrackSpeedGrowth exist for. Hitter confirms nobody else was hitting nearby during this session, so the impulse is NOT another player's bat. Measured per octave it carries 86% of its energy between 250 Hz and 2 kHz and 0.2% above 4 kHz, against 11-14% above 4 kHz for a verified crack — a loud, sharp, band-limited thump (bat on the ground, a bag, a foot on a board). It is the one clip that still fires at the shipped 6 kHz / 30 dB setting, at exactly 30.0 dB.

clips.label: no_swing
clips.notes: Hitter: 'Swing 1. Session, false positive, 6m away.' Published 10.1 deg at 4.8 mph from a blob drifting at 0.075 diameters a frame — the clip minDiametersPerFrame exists for.

clips.label: no_swing
clips.notes: Hitter: 'Swing 3 session false positive 6m away. This one did not even calculate.' Recorded with the Camera app. Detected here by the Python reference detector, not on the phone — no on-device trace was ever exported. Drops roughly a quarter of its frames. Replayed WITHOUT a contact time, because none was ever recorded for it — so this row exercises the imported-clip path, where there is no audio trigger, and not the path the phone took when it declined to calculate.

clips.contact_source: video: the pitch track and the hit track crossing
clips.label: hit
clips.notes: Hitter-confirmed HIT, filmed at 6 m with the Camera app. The clip carries its own scale: the incoming pitch is a long ballistic arc of the same ball at the same distance, and its vertical acceleration gives metres-per-pixel without measuring the ball's size at all. Gravity says the ball is 21.96 px across (camera 5.57 m); this is the ground truth the diameter probe is scored against. These are the FIRST hitter-confirmed positives in the corpus — every gate and threshold before them was tuned only against clips whose right answer was 'no'.
